existing.description: Berea College plans to move to a fully funded program model for all students by fall 2027, expanding its tuition-free approach to cover housing and meal plans with no student loans.
eligibility: Apply as a first-year student to Berea College
Meet the College's financial eligibility requirement, assessed from the FAFSA using household size and adjusted gross income
Show strong academic accomplishments; admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA
Come from a family with limited financial resources; most admitted families have an annual household income within the range of the federal poverty guidelines
Domestic applicants must use the 1 November, 31 January or 31 March cycle; international applicants the 15 October or 15 January dates
All applicants must submit a FAFSA to be considered for admission
existing.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants, domestic or international, who show strong academic accomplishments and come from families with limited financial resources and who meet Berea's financial eligibility requirement, which the College assesses from the FAFSA using household size and adjusted gross income bands. Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants. Every applicant must submit a FAFSA to be considered for admission.
benefits: Guaranteed tuition coverage after all other grants and scholarships are applied
Published 2026-27 tuition of $56,900 eliminated for the student
Free laptop issued to each accepted student, which the student keeps after graduation
Average $4,000 provided per student for an internship experience
Guaranteed on-campus job through the Work College Program, required of every student
$400 stipend for professional clothing for juniors and seniors
Study abroad opportunities and relocation funds after graduation
From Fall 2027, 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies covered without loans
coverage: Remaining cost of tuition after all federal, state, institutional and private grants and scholarships are considered, so the student never pays tuition from personal income
From Fall 2027, extension of coverage to 100% of housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students until graduation
requirements: File the FAFSA, which is required for admission consideration because of Berea's financial eligibility requirement, and refile it every year while enrolled
Apply within the advised cycle, with Early Action strongly recommended because admission is selective and space is limited

Meet the minimum admissions criteria, which the catalog describes as an ACT composite of 19 or SAT of 980 and ranking in the top three-fifths of the high school class, though the College is test-optional
Submit the School Counselor Evaluation Form unless you hold a GED or are home-schooled
Submit one teacher recommendation from a core subject
Complete the application in full, as incomplete applications are not considered
If requested, complete the Non-Custodial Financial Questionnaire or provide additional financial documentation
documents: Application for Admission and Scholarship, submitted free of charge
Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
School Counselor Evaluation Form, not required for GED holders and home-school applicants
One teacher recommendation from a core subject teacher
ACT or SAT scores, unless applying test-optional
Non-Custodial Financial Questionnaire, Self-Employed/Business Owner Questionnaire or additional documentation, if requested during financial eligibility assessment
existing.english_requirement: Not specified on the Berea Tuition Promise pages. International applicants are welcomed and must meet the College's general admission requirements; the College states it welcomes applicants "from across the United States and from other countries".
application_method: Complete the Application for Admission and Scholarship online at the Berea admissions portal at no cost
File the FAFSA, which the FAFSA becomes available each October 1
Ask a high school guidance counsellor to complete the School Counselor Evaluation Form, unless exempt
Ask a core subject teacher to submit the teacher recommendation
Submit by the applicable Early Action or Regular Decision date for domestic or international applicants
Complete any additional financial documentation the Office of Admissions requests during the financial eligibility assessment
existing.selection_notes: The admissions process is holistic, weighing the completed application, official academic records, test scores where submitted, financial eligibility, recommendations and endorsements, conversations with an admissions counsellor, extracurricular and co-curricular activity, community service, character and personal qualities, and demonstrated interest in the College. Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants, and Berea is academically competitive with an average ACT of about 25 and more than half of first-year students ranked in the top fifth of their high school class. Well qualified applicants may be accepted for fall admission as early as December, though an early application alone does not ensure admission.
existing.best_fit: Students with strong academic potential from families with limited financial resources who want a tuition-free bachelor's degree at a work college in Kentucky, and who are willing to meet Berea's unique financial eligibility test.
existing.notes: This is not a competitive merit award that applicants win. Berea has not charged tuition for more than 130 years, and the Tuition Promise Scholarship is applied after all other aid is considered, so every admitted student receives it. It is awarded to admitted students rather than at application stage, which matters for applicants who assume they must win it. Housing, food and fees remain payable for current cohorts, but from Fall 2027 the College's Financial Freedom Pledge guarantees 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students until graduation. Endowment earnings provide 74% of the College's operating budget, state and federal aid 19% and donors the remaining 7%.
existing.duration: Four years, renewed annually while the student remains enrolled and files the FAFSA each year
existing.application_period: Rolling admission with three advised domestic first-year deadlines each cycle: Early Action I on 1 November, Early Action II on 31 January and Regular Decision on 31 March. International applicants use 15 October for Early Action and 15 January for Regular Decision. The FAFSA is refiled every year, available from 1 October with a 31 October priority date.
existing.deadline_display: Official wording for first-year domestic applicants: "Early Action I: November 1", "Early Action II: January 31", "Regular Decision: March 31". International applicants may apply by October 15 for Early Action or January 15 for Regular Decision. Berea advises that "Applying by the Early Action deadlines is highly recommended, as admission is selective and space in the incoming class is limited." All applicants must also submit a FAFSA, which is available from October 1 with an expected priority filing date of October 31.
existing.program_type: Need-aware tuition promise awarded to all admitted students, not a competitive merit scholarship

existing.funding_period: per fellowship term, paid in two equal instalments
existing.description: AAUW's International Fellowships fund international women pursuing graduate study in STEM disciplines in the United States, with the intention of applying their expertise and leadership in service of their home countries. The programme has supported international women in full-time postgraduate study in the United States since 1917. Each award carries a stipend of USD 20,000 for a master's degree or USD 25,000 for a doctorate, disbursed in two equal payments at the beginning and midpoint of the term. A limited number of awards are also available for study in a country other than the applicant's own, under stated conditions. The 2027-28 application window ran from August 17 to September 17, 2026 and has now closed.
eligibility: Applicants must identify as a woman.
Applicants must be admitted or enrolled in their first master's or an academic or professional doctorate degree at the time of application, and the degree must be in one of the STEM disciplines.
Applicants must begin their program on or before September 15, 2027, and complete it on or after April 30, 2028.
Applicants must possess at least one academic degree (earned in the U.S. or abroad) that is equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree.
Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned.
Applicants may apply for only one degree type (either a Master's or Doctoral program) and in a single specific field.
Applicants must pursue their study in the U.S. on a full-time basis at an institution accredited by the U.S. Department of Education.
Fellowship recipients must be non-U.S. citizens and must not hold U.S. permanent resident status, nor be applicants for U.S. permanent residency (green card).

Study outside the U.S. is considered only for applicants whose country of citizenship is subject to a U.S. travel ban and who cannot secure a U.S. student visa, or who are not travel-banned, plan to study outside the United States, and are members of Graduate Women International.
existing.eligibility_summary: Women who are non-U.S. citizens and not U.S. permanent residents, admitted or enrolled in a first master's or academic/professional doctorate in a STEM discipline at an accredited U.S. institution, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale.
benefits: Stipend of USD 20,000 for a master's degree
Stipend of USD 25,000 for a doctorate degree
Stipends are payable to fellows only and disbursed in two equal payments at the beginning and the midpoint of the fellowship term
coverage: Cash stipend paid directly to the fellow
Two equal stipend payments at the beginning and midpoint of the fellowship term
requirements: A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned
Full-time study at a U.S. Department of Education accredited institution
Program start on or before September 15, 2027 and completion on or after April 30, 2028
documents: Online narrative application submitted through the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal
Two letters of recommendation from advisors, professors, colleagues or others academically or professionally familiar with the applicant
Official transcripts and degree documentation supporting the GPA claim
Evidence of admission to or enrolment in the qualifying degree programme
application_method: Create an account or log in to the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal
Register recommenders early so each receives a personalised submission link
Submit the narrative application and all supporting documents before the deadline; the application is incomplete until recommendations are submitted
existing.selection_notes: Applications are read against published selection criteria for master's and doctoral degree tracks, covering demonstrated academic or scholarly excellence, feasibility of the proposed academic, professional or research plan, and the applicant's potential to advance the fellowship's mission.
existing.best_fit: Women who are non-U.S. citizens or permanent residents, hold a first master's or doctoral place at an accredited U.S. institution in a formally classified STEM programme, and have a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or above.
existing.notes: A two-year renewal may be awarded to up to five master's degree candidates, conditional on a minimum 3.5 GPA in the first year plus a funding renewal form, official transcript and institutional certification form by May 30, 2027.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. The 2027-28 window ran from August 17, 2026, 9:00am ET to September 17, 2026, 5:00pm ET; award notification March 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications closed September 17, 2026, at 5:00pm ET for the 2027-28 academic year. AAUW states: 'Applications have closed for the 2027-28 academic year.'
existing.program_type: Graduate fellowship for international women pursuing STEM degrees
